distillation_scope.disease_name_scope: Pure disease-name distillation. No severity subtype, transmission setting, complication, or mimic was added to the disease name.
distillation_scope.leaf_granularity: First-layer disease leaf for acute HAV infection; acute liver failure, cholestatic hepatitis, relapsing course, acalculous cholecystitis, renal injury, and pregnancy/host vulnerability are represented as mechanisms, axes, event hazards, or risk modifiers.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: HAV fecal-oral exposure and hepatotropic replication
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Acquisition of hepatitis A virus through fecal-oral exposure followed by intestinal amplification, viremia, hepatocyte/Kupffer-cell infection, biliary excretion, and stool shedding.

Innate antiviral and inflammatory response causing fever, chills, malaise, fatigue, headache, myalgia, anorexia, nausea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort, and diarrhea before or during the icteric phase.
Cytotoxic T-cell and innate immune injury to infected hepatocytes, producing abrupt hepatocellular transaminitis, hepatic tenderness, jaundice, and usually self-limited recovery.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Canalicular cholestasis and bile ductular reaction
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Inflammatory disruption of bile secretion and ductular reaction causing direct-predominant hyperbilirubinemia, pruritus, dark urine, acholic stool, alkaline phosphatase/GGT elevation, and prolonged cholestatic hepatitis.

Severe hepatocyte loss or dysfunction causing INR rise, low albumin contribution, impaired ammonia handling, hepatic encephalopathy, hypoglycemia risk, bleeding vulnerability, and acute liver failure physiology.

Immune complex, complement, endothelial, hemodynamic, and pigment/cholestasis-associated injury producing AKI, proteinuria/hematuria, hemolysis-like findings, bleeding lesions, and rare neurologic endothelial complications.

HAV-related hepatic and biliary inflammation with hypoalbuminemia or local edema causing gallbladder wall thickening, hydropic distension, pericholecystic fluid, periportal edema, Murphy sign, and acalculous cholecystitis mimicry.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Prolonged or relapsing HAV immune activity
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Delayed resolution or biphasic immune activity causing recurrent symptoms, persistent jaundice, continued stool HAV RNA shedding, and slowly resolving cholestatic hepatitis despite falling transaminases.
Rare severe HAV course where hepatic failure, renal failure, coagulopathy, bleeding, infection vulnerability, transplant physiology, or ICU complications drive mortality.

mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Acute HAV infection induces detectable anti-HAV IgM during symptomatic illness.
HAV replicates and is excreted in stool, sometimes after viremia resolves.
Viremia may be detectable around the incubation and early symptomatic phase.
Hepatotropic replication provides antigenic substrate for immune-mediated hepatocellular injury.
Early viral infection drives systemic inflammatory symptoms.
Compatible fecal-oral exposure increases the prior probability of HAV infection.
Lack of HAV immunity leaves the host susceptible after exposure.
Fever is common early in symptomatic acute HAV.
Systemic cytokine response raises measured temperature when observed during febrile phase.
Fatigue and malaise are prominent constitutional symptoms.
Nausea and vomiting are common in acute hepatitis A.
Poor appetite is a common prodromal and icteric symptom.
Myalgia and aches occur with systemic viral inflammation.
Headache can accompany febrile acute HAV.
HAV may produce gastrointestinal symptoms including diarrhea.
Acute hepatocyte injury releases ALT, often into the hundreds to thousands.
Acute hepatocyte injury releases AST in parallel with ALT.
Hepatic inflammation can cause RUQ or epigastric discomfort.
Inflamed liver capsule can be tender or painful.
Acute hepatitis may cause mild hepatomegaly.
Hepatocellular dysfunction and cholestasis raise bilirubin.
Clinically visible jaundice emerges as bilirubin rises.
Intrahepatic cholestasis causes direct-predominant bilirubin elevation.
Canalicular and ductular inflammation raises alkaline phosphatase variably.
GGT may rise with cholestatic acute HAV.
Bile salt and cholestatic mediator retention produces itching.
Conjugated bilirubin causes dark urine.
Reduced bile pigment delivery can cause pale stool.
Persistent cholestatic activity drives the atypical prolonged cholestasis course.
Biphasic immune activity can produce recurrent symptoms and liver enzyme abnormalities.
Persistent liver infection can sustain stool RNA shedding after blood PCR is negative.
Loss of hepatic synthetic function prolongs INR.
Severe or prolonged hepatic illness can lower serum albumin, though albumin also reflects nutrition and inflammation.
Severe hepatic dysfunction impairs ammonia metabolism.
Hyperammonemia and liver failure produce hepatic encephalopathy.
Synthetic failure plus encephalopathy is the acute liver failure event chain.
HAV-associated AKI raises serum creatinine.
AKI or dehydration raises BUN.
Immune-mediated renal involvement can produce proteinuria.
HAV-associated renal involvement can produce hematuria.
Renal immune/endothelial injury and dehydration can produce AKI.
Severe AKI, hypertension, and endothelial injury can create PRES vulnerability.
HAV-related gallbladder edema thickens the wall without stones.
Wall thickness is a measurable expression of gallbladder edema.
A hydropic gallbladder can occur in HAV-related acalculous inflammation.
Pericholecystic fluid can reflect local edema and inflammation.
Acute hepatitis may produce periportal edema or hypodensity on imaging.
Gallbladder inflammation can produce a Murphy sign despite absent stones.
The edema/inflammation pattern can cross into true HAV-associated acalculous cholecystitis.
Severe coagulopathy, vascular injury, and procedures increase bleeding risk.
Mortality rises when HAV progresses to liver failure, renal failure, bleeding, or ICU complications.
HAV-related acute liver failure is the main lethal pathway.
AKI worsens reserve and complicates fluid, ammonia, and transplant management.
Major hemorrhage in the setting of hepatic failure can be fatal.

Measured body temperature at the observation snapshot.
Heart rate reflecting fever, dehydration, pain, bleeding, or critical illness.

Mean arterial pressure derived from blood pressure.

Arthralgia or joint aches during HAV prodrome.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: AST and ALT rise together from hepatocellular injury, with individual ratios varying.
HAV jaundice is often direct-predominant, especially with cholestasis.
Higher direct and total bilirubin make jaundice more visible.
Conjugated bilirubin excretion causes dark urine.
ALP and GGT often move together in cholestatic HAV but may be less extreme than bilirubin.
Rising INR is a central sign of severe hepatic synthetic failure.
Hyperammonemia increases encephalopathy hazard in ALF.
Encephalopathy plus coagulopathy defines the critical ALF pathway.
Severe or persistent AKI may require renal replacement therapy.
Severe AKI and labile hypertension can increase PRES hazard.
Wall edema and pericholecystic fluid often co-occur in acalculous cholecystitis but are not mandatory together.
Marked wall thickening with symptoms increases the acalculous cholecystitis event hazard.
Severe coagulopathy increases bleeding hazard, especially with procedures or ulcers.
Acute liver failure is the dominant mortality pathway in HAV.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Hydration helps prerenal injury but severe AKI narrows the safe fluid window.

treatments.context_specific_role: Maintains perfusion, oral intake, and symptom control while the HAV immune course resolves.
Reduces avoidable hepatic stress during acute HAV recovery.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Vitamin K cannot reverse INR caused by severe hepatocyte synthetic failure.
Cholestasis and poor intake can produce a vitamin K-responsive component.

treatments.context_specific_role: Tests and treats a deficiency component of coagulopathy without masking the need to evaluate ALF.
Includes agents such as ursodeoxycholic acid or bile-acid binding approaches when prolonged cholestatic symptoms dominate.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Persistent extrahepatic obstruction needs evaluation rather than immune suppression.

treatments.context_specific_role: Reserved structurally for refractory prolonged cholestasis after competing obstruction/chronic liver disease is evaluated.
Adjunctive liver support when HAV course approaches severe acute liver injury or ALF physiology.
Serial mental status, glucose, INR, ammonia, renal, bleeding, airway, and cerebral edema monitoring in HAV ALF.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Dialysis or CRRT requires equipment, access, and monitoring.
Vascular access and anticoagulation decisions are harder during severe coagulopathy.

treatments.context_specific_role: Supports severe AKI, volume, acidosis, uremia, or hyperammonemia context during critical HAV.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Benefit depends on candidacy, center access, timing, and organ availability.
AKI raises urgency and post-transplant risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Rescue pathway for HAV acute liver failure with poor-prognosis physiology.
Observation, fluids, symptom control, imaging follow-up, and surgery/source-control escalation only if complications emerge.
Reduces transmission and protects contacts; it is not expected to reverse the index patient's liver injury.

present.trajectory_modulation: Raises susceptibility after exposure; does not by itself determine severity.
Raises prior probability for HAV among acute febrile jaundice illnesses.
Adults are more likely to be symptomatic and more vulnerable to severe jaundice, ALF, and prolonged recovery than young children.
Reduces hepatic reserve and raises risk from HAV hepatocellular injury.
Raises monitoring concern for dehydration, cholestasis, fetal/maternal reserve, and liver failure mimicry.
Amplifies AKI hazard and may worsen hypotension, tachycardia, nausea, and hospitalization need.
Raises creatinine background and AKI/dialysis vulnerability during HAV.
Prolongs jaundice, pruritus, direct bilirubin, and outpatient follow-up burden.
May alter symptom expression, viral shedding, post-transplant infectious risk, and tolerance of rescue immunosuppression.

supportive_care: Structure diagnosis around compatible acute febrile/gastrointestinal prodrome, jaundice, marked hepatocellular transaminitis, bilirubin pattern, and HAV IgM or HAV RNA evidence.
Trend AST, ALT, total/direct bilirubin, ALP, GGT, INR, glucose, albumin, creatinine/BUN, urine output, and mental status rather than relying on a single peak.
Escalate monitoring when INR rises, encephalopathy appears, glucose falls, ammonia rises, creatinine rises, urine output falls, bleeding occurs, or transaminases remain extreme.

Interpret gallbladder wall thickening, hydropic gallbladder, pericholecystic fluid, and RUQ tenderness as possible HAV biliary edema/acalculous cholecystitis, while still checking for stones, obstruction, bacterial cholecystitis, and cholangitis when clinically indicated.

For prolonged cholestasis, preserve high direct bilirubin, pruritus, dark urine, acholic stool, imaging exclusion of obstruction, and time course as rankable evidence rather than replacing the disease with generic obstruction.
Avoid alcohol, unnecessary acetaminophen, hepatotoxic drugs, NSAIDs when coagulopathic, and dehydration during acute illness.
Use enteric precautions, public-health reporting where required, contact review, and post-exposure vaccination or immune globulin decisions for contacts according to local policy.
Do not let HAV IgG alone label acute disease; acute disease needs IgM, HAV RNA, or a compatible acute course.
Separate acute hepatitis A from acute liver failure as a complication path: HAV is the disease manifold; acute liver failure is an event hazard that can dominate RMST when present.
When ALF physiology appears, involve hepatology/transplant and critical care early while continuing to preserve HAV-specific evidence and excluding competing causes.
quality_notes: No treatment ranking label fields are used.
Acalculous cholecystitis, prolonged cholestasis, renal injury, PRES, and ALF are represented as event/context axes, not disease-name qualifiers.
